deities: Mahalakshmi (Adishakti, peaceful/Satvika form, idol wears a Shiva linga on head)

history.dynasty: Shilahara rulers (750–1030 CE) and early Kadamba kings of Goa (worship of the goddess); present temple established 1866
history.period: Present structure 1866 CE; worship tradition much older (attested 1413 onwards in popular accounts)
history.summary: The goddess Mahalakshmi was revered by the Shilahara rulers and early Kadamba kings; Portuguese records list a Mahalaxmi (Malcumi) temple destroyed in 1567. Devotees Safto and Fato smuggled the original idol from Colva (Salcette) to Talauli and then to Bandivade, where it was installed beside the existing Bandivade idol — so the temple holds two Mahalaxmi idols plus idols of the two devotees. The present temple was established in 1866; its sabhamandapa holds a noted gallery of 22–24 wooden Vishnu/Bhagavata panels and a medieval monolithic deepastamba. CSV CORRECTION: actual town is Bandora (Bandivade), Ponda taluka — NOT Margao; district North Goa. POSSIBLE DUPLICATE: CSV row 227 (Shree Mahalaxmi Temple, Vasco da Gama) very likely describes this same famous temple; investigate and dedup.

name: Shri Mahalakshmi Temple
town_description: Bandora (also Bandivade) is a temple-dotted village in Ponda taluka, North Goa, about 4 km from Ponda town and 5 minutes from the famous Shantadurga temple at Kavale. It is a traditional GSB religious centre, home to several historic shrines including Ramnath and Mahalakshmi temples.

travel.road: About 4 km from Ponda; 27 km from Panjim Kadamba Bus Stand

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navaratri for the grandest celebrations
